_note: The school model (GDD 4.9.3, session S1; scripts/core/school_system.gd). The calendar itself (real 2026-27 dates and the rules for later years) is data/school.json; this file holds the model: the stages, the subjects, the starting grades by the creation answer, how grades drift, the tests, the report cards and the life load (session L1b: the two old weekly life settings, study effort and free time, became the free-time slots and the standing habits of data/habits.json). NEUTRAL = IDENTICAL: a normal school day with the default habit has a life load of exactly 0, and at 0 the game is today's game to the last digit (the code does not even run). Life load is a number per day in 'points': positive = a heavier day (fatigue recovers slower, colds a little more likely, injuries a little more likely), negative = a lighter one (holidays). All numbers here are Claude's first guesses (estimated), to be tuned in B1; the user's decisions of 2026-10-17 are in GDD 4.9.3 'Built (step S1)'.

stages._note: The school year that starts in the autumn of year Y is grade Y - birth year - grade_offset (born 2012: grade 8 in 2026-27). Grades 8 and 9 are yläkoulu (`list`); from the school year in which the athlete would be in grade 10 (born 2012: autumn 2028) the stage comes from the athlete's PATH (SchoolSystem.paths, made by the application, GDD 4.9.3 session S3a) and is one of `secondary` below. `scale` multiplies every positive part of the life load (grade 9 has more homework); `exam_weeks` = the stage's big exam weeks (user 2026-10-17: none in yläkoulu, only single tests). Rule formats: {before: christmas | winter | end, weeks: n} = the Mon-Fri school week n weeks before that break's first free day; {periods: true, last_shift_days: -2} = the last `exam_week_school_days` school days of each lukio period (data/school.json rules.lukio_periods, fitted to Helsingin kielilukio 2026-27; the last period's exam week ends `last_shift_days` days before the year's end). `applies`: the joint application is made in this stage's spring. `years`: how long a path of this kind lasts by default (session S3b: a lukio can take 3 or 4 years, the player's choice in the lukio's first stop, stored on the path; courses and the matriculation exams: data/lukio.json). `final`: the last year of a path (the final certificate).

subjects._note: The yläkoulu subjects of the report card (GDD 4.9.3). academic = the subjects of the application average (lukuaineet, S3); practical subjects are graded from the term's work without tests. In real schools music, art, crafts and home economics are partly electives in grades 8-9; S1 keeps them all on the card as the GDD lists them.

answers._note: The creation answer 'How do you do at school?' (background_questions.json school_answer): `start` = the starting grade average (GDD 4.9.3: ~9.0 / 8.5 / 7.5 / 6.8 / 6.3), `natural` = the average the grades drift to at Normal effort. 'Good grades through hard work' starts above its natural level (keeping it costs more effort); 'Couldn't care less' a little below (unused talent). Older saves have only school_level: `from_level` maps it.

aptitude._note: Each subject has a hidden aptitude: the subject's natural level = the answer's natural average + a roll (normal, sd, at most max away), re-centred so the academic subjects (and the practical ones) average the answer's level exactly. PE: + pe_bonus (an athlete), + sports_class with the 'A sports class at school' answer. Rolled once from the career's own dice (name + birth date; the global dice untouched).

grades._note: Every school day each subject's level drifts towards its target: level += (target - level) x (1 - 0.5^(1 / half_life_days)), so half the way in half_life_days school days (~a school year). target = natural + the study slots' shift (session L1b: data/habits.json effects, +-1 at most like the old Heavy / Light effort; 0 with the default habit) + focus shift, kept inside min..max. GDD 4.9.7 targets: the default holds the average +-0.3 a year, a shift of +1 gives +0.5 a year, -1 gives -0.5 (= half of the shift in a year). Focus subjects (at most focus_max): + focus_shift each; every other academic subject - focus_others per focus subject (the study time moves).

tests._note: Single tests (kokeet): each academic subject has per_term tests a term (autumn: the start to the Christmas break; spring: after Christmas to the end), placed at even points of the term's school days plus a roll (jitter_sd school days), never in the first skip_days school days. Tests cluster naturally around the same points (like period ends). With an exam week in the term (S3), each subject's last test moves into it. A test's score = level + a roll (noise_sd) - stress (from stress_from: up to stress_penalty at 100), kept inside 4..10, rounded to round_to (8+ = 8.25, 8½, 9- = 8.75). The week's tests: more than normal_per_week tests in a Mon-Sun week make it a busy test week (life load on its test days, stress).

report_cards._note: A report card on the last school day before the Christmas break (`christmas`) and on the last day of the school year (`spring`; in grade 9 the final certificate, `final`). Academic subjects: round(tests_weight x the term's test average + (1 - tests_weight) x the level), practical subjects: round(level); whole grades 4-10. The card keeps `average` (every subject) and `academic_average` (the application average of S3).

life_load._note: The day's life load, in points (0 = a normal school day with the default habit = today's game). Parts: a weekday off school in a break or the summer (holiday_weekday; user 2026-10-17: holidays = relief), and on SCHOOL days only: the free-time slots (session L1b, data/habits.json: extra study in the week, a late night after a friends evening, an early night after a rest evening; they replaced the two old settings study effort and free time), a double day = two separate practices (two sessions that are not add-ons; drills, strides and the like ride along in the same practice, so the coach's Monday 'easy run + drills' is no double day), each test on a day of a busy test week, a day of an exam week (S3). Weekends are 0. Positive parts x the stage's scale. Double days are free on holidays and weekends (and in S3 in the urheilulukio's morning-practice slots).

effects._note: What the life load does (user 2026-10-17: mild). Fatigue: the day's keep (the share of fatigue carried to tomorrow, Training.daily_keep) + keep_per_point x load (an exam day of 2 points: ~4 % more fatigue built up over a week). Colds: the day's chance x (1 + illness_per_point x load), never below illness_min. Injuries (overuse and bad-luck): x (1 + injury_per_point x load) for a positive load only (Mann 2016, Hamlin 2019: more injuries in academic-stress weeks; older athletes than ours, so mild). Stress: the Sunday drift's pull = the coming week's life load summed over its days / 7 x stress_per_point; holidays pull it down. Busy test week ahead: stress news busy_week_news on the Sunday before (exam week ahead: exam_week_news). Motivation: the free-time slots' pull is in data/habits.json (session L1b; it was free time's motivation_lots / motivation_little here).

decisions._note: The school's decisions (GDD 4.9.3, session S2), only in the real game (SchoolSystem.decisions_enabled, set by main.gd: the tools that play days never see them). 'meet_test': a stop on the morning a race you entered is in a week where tests clash with it (a busy test week with at least min_left_busy tests still to write up to the race day, or a test on the race day or the day before it): three answers. Each option: test_penalty = grades off every test written in that Mon-Sun week, load = extra life load points on each school day of that week (x the stage's scale), stress = news to the stress mood when chosen, scratch = the race is withdrawn. Claude's first guesses (estimated), tuned in B1. An answer that is not an option id (a tool's 'ok') = `default`.

meet_test.title: Tests and a race this week
meet_test.text: You still have {tests} to write ({list}), and you are racing at {meet} {when}. You can't give both everything. What do you do?

options.label: Race and risk the grades
options.detail: Your tests this week come out about half a grade lower. Nothing else changes.
options.note: You race and hope the tests go well enough: this week's tests will cost you a little.

options.label: Study and scratch the race
options.detail: You withdraw from the race. The tests go as usual and the week is calmer.

options.label: Race and study on the bus
options.detail: Tests only a little lower, but the school days weigh more and you get stressed: more tiredness, more colds.
options.note: You race and study on the bus: a heavy week.

card._note: The report card day (session S2): a stop with the card (SchoolEventPanel) and, after it, the choice for the next term: keep my evenings, one more study evening or one fewer (session L1b: the choice edits the habits by one slot; its texts are in data/habits.json card); only the options that change something are offered. The final certificate has just Continue. Verdict = the average against the previous card (`delta`), level = the average now. The family's reaction comes with the people system (P1).

ui._note: Everything the player reads in the school UI (session S2): the School page (People tab), the week strip, the day editor's blocks, the Calendar bands and the Report tab. {x} = a value filled in by the code. (Session L1b: the two settings' texts are gone; the habits' are in data/habits.json ui.)
ui.page_note: School changes how heavy your days are and how your grades go. It never changes what you train.
ui.week_busy: A busy test week: the school days weigh more.
ui.focus_text: Push up to two subjects: they rise faster while the other subjects slip a little. Change them any time; grades move slowly, so switching back and forth gains nothing.
ui.focus_full: Two focus subjects already: tap one to drop it first.
ui.grades_text: Where you stand in each subject, written the way tests are in Finland: 8, 8+, 8½, 9-. Tap a subject for its latest tests.
ui.avg_note: The academic subjects and PE are what you apply with: the joint application after grade 9 counts their average.
